title: An application you grow by talking to it
provenance_policy: Show capture provenance in every evidence scene. Scripted deterministic kernel evidence must never be labeled as model-generated chat. Illustrations are explanatory diagrams. Never invent model replies.

videos.title: What actually happens when you ask?

scenes.title: A request becomes a concrete operation
scenes.narration: You type: let me record an expense with an amount and category. The model sees the application catalogue and the tools available to it. A request can become development, execution, or inspection.

visual.description: A request becomes a concrete operation
visual.headline: A request becomes a concrete operation
visual.caption: Explanatory diagram

scenes.title: The application starts with a small contract
scenes.narration: Our example starts with a ledger and caller-owned checks. Amounts are integer cents. Categories describe each entry. Expense functions are absent, so the first request really adds a capability to this application.

visual.description: The application starts with a small contract
visual.headline: The application starts with a small contract
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: A definition becomes a reusable function
scenes.narration: The controller submits a Lisp definition through the development tool. The worker evaluates it inside the application. Once accepted, the function appears in the catalogue, with its arguments, documentation, and source available for inspection.

visual.description: A definition becomes a reusable function
visual.headline: A definition becomes a reusable function
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: Calling the function changes managed state
scenes.narration: Now call add-expense with four hundred fifty cents and coffee. The worker updates the managed ledger. This is an execution of a real function. Its accepted state can be stored and recovered later.

visual.description: Calling the function changes managed state
visual.headline: Calling the function changes managed state

scenes.title: Read the accumulated application state
scenes.narration: Add groceries and transport, then ask for a total. The new total-expenses function reads the same ledger. The result is five thousand four hundred fifty cents: fifty-four dollars and fifty cents.

scenes.title: Compose ordinary Lisp functions
scenes.narration: A budget report can call total-expenses and spending-by-category. It does not need another special pipeline language. The application grows a vocabulary of useful functions that you, or the conversational controller, can reuse.

scenes.title: Make the machinery inspectable
scenes.narration: Inspect the catalogue, read a function, and review operation history. Operations record attempts; revisions identify accepted code or data changes. An unsuccessful attempt can be useful evidence without becoming a new application version.

visual.description: Make the machinery inspectable
visual.headline: Make the machinery inspectable
visual.caption: Explanatory diagram

scenes.title: Keep accepted work across sessions
scenes.narration: Closing the process ends its active calls. Reopening the same workspace recovers accepted managed code and data. Conversation memory has its own lifetime. The useful artifact you have built is the evolving Lisp application.

visual.description: Keep accepted work across sessions
visual.headline: Keep accepted work across sessions
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: A controller outside, a worker inside
scenes.narration: Jiti is a cooperative live image repair kernel for SBCL. An external controller proposes actions. One owning worker evaluates application forms and retains live restarts when a condition pauses an attempt. This separation lets the controller inspect and repair a call without moving its restart to another thread.

visual.description: A controller outside, a worker inside
visual.headline: A controller outside, a worker inside
visual.caption: Explanatory diagram

scenes.title: The world adapter defines what is managed
scenes.narration: An application supplies a world adapter: an evaluation package, observations, checkpoints, restoration, and a catalogue. Durable export and import make managed state recoverable. The reference adapter covers readable table values and supported named function definitions. An application with other resources needs corresponding adapter coverage.

visual.description: The world adapter defines what is managed
visual.headline: The world adapter defines what is managed
visual.caption: Explanatory diagram

scenes.title: A small foundation, then incremental definitions
scenes.narration: The expense example starts with an empty ledger and executable caller checks. It has no expense functions. Development adds add-expense, total-expenses, spending-by-category, and budget-report in stages. The source is inspectable, and each accepted definition becomes available to later calls.

visual.description: A small foundation, then incremental definitions
visual.headline: A small foundation, then incremental definitions
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: Goals and safety answer different questions
scenes.narration: A goal asks whether we have reached the desired behavior. A safety invariant asks whether an intermediate state is acceptable. A false goal can coexist with an accepted development step. A false or signaled invariant rejects the attempt and restores its managed checkpoint. The caller owns both contracts.

visual.description: Goals and safety answer different questions
visual.headline: Goals and safety answer different questions
lines: False goal → may keep safe progress
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: One provisional checkpoint covers the attempt
scenes.narration: The worker checkpoints managed state before reading, compiling, and evaluating a form. Repairs performed while that attempt is paused share its provisional checkpoint. If repair evaluation fails, the entire attempt is aborted. This makes code changes and data changes participate in the same managed rollback boundary.

visual.description: One provisional checkpoint covers the attempt
visual.headline: One provisional checkpoint covers the attempt
visual.caption: Explanatory diagram

scenes.title: Operations, revisions, and generations differ
scenes.narration: Each attempt has an operation identity for diagnostics. A revision identifies accepted managed code or data. Pure calls and final-state no-ops do not create revisions. Observation generations coordinate worker actions and reject stale commands. These identifiers serve different purposes, even when one interaction displays all three.

visual.description: Operations, revisions, and generations differ
visual.headline: Operations, revisions, and generations differ
visual.caption: Explanatory diagram

scenes.title: Preview restores managed code and data
scenes.narration: Preview evaluates an operation and returns bounded printable results, then restores the checkpoint. Its restoration also covers repairs made during a pause. Ordinary execution can retain safe changes instead. Preview only covers managed effects; an adapter cannot retract an email or network request simply by restoring its ledger.

visual.description: Preview restores managed code and data
visual.headline: Preview restores managed code and data
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: Rollback publishes a new point in history
scenes.narration: After a change is accepted, rollback can restore an older managed revision. It publishes a new revision rather than erasing the intervening history. This is different from preview, which does not retain the temporary change. Rollback restores application code and data, not a historical call stack.

visual.description: Rollback publishes a new point in history
visual.headline: Rollback publishes a new point in history
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: A condition exposes live restart choices
scenes.narration: Here a report encounters a category its label helper cannot handle. The worker pauses inside the active call and exposes restart choices. The operation identity remains the same. Its local marker and entry counter give us concrete evidence about which frame continues when we repair and resume.

visual.description: A condition exposes live restart choices
visual.headline: A condition exposes live restart choices
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: Resume the original frame after repairing a helper
scenes.narration: We replace the category helper and also define a new report body. Resuming through the live restart completes the existing invocation with its original frame marker. A subsequent report call enters the new body and increments the counter again. Global dispatch can see new helpers; existing frames retain their bodies.

visual.description: Resume the original frame after repairing a helper
visual.headline: Resume the original frame after repairing a helper
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: Durable recovery starts a fresh process
scenes.narration: Persistence records immutable world artifacts and a current revision pointer. Recovery imports the accepted revision into a fresh process. It does not replay old actions or recreate suspended stacks. Unfinished operations become interrupted diagnostics. The recovered expense functions still read the recovered ledger and produce the same totals.

visual.description: Durable recovery starts a fresh process
visual.headline: Durable recovery starts a fresh process
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: An inspectable experiment in live development
scenes.narration: The kernel relies on cooperative application code and accurate world adapters. Arbitrary hostile Lisp and unmanaged resources are beyond its guarantees. What the demo makes concrete is incremental development with caller-owned checks, accepted history, and a live repair path. Run it, inspect its evidence, and adapt the world to your application.

visual.description: An inspectable experiment in live development
visual.headline: An inspectable experiment in live development
visual.caption: Explanatory diagram

scenes.title: Preview a temporary change
scenes.narration: Preview adding another expense. You can inspect the temporary result, then the managed ledger returns to its earlier state. The trial does not become an accepted revision.

visual.headline: Preview a temporary change

scenes.title: Accept a change into history
scenes.narration: Execute a change normally and let caller checks validate it. Safe managed changes can become an accepted revision. Operation history records the attempt; revision history records the new application state. These histories tell different parts of the story.

visual.description: Accept a change into history
visual.headline: Accept a change into history
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: Restore earlier state and preserve history
scenes.narration: Now roll back to the earlier revision. Jiti restores its managed definitions and data and publishes another revision. The intervening history remains inspectable. Preview is for trying a change; rollback is for restoring an already accepted state.

visual.description: Restore earlier state and preserve history
visual.headline: Restore earlier state and preserve history
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.narration: A report starts with the local marker v-one active frame. Its entry counter is one. It then encounters a transport category its helper cannot label.

scenes.title: The worker holds the active restart
scenes.narration: The condition pauses the attempt and exposes a live restart. The owning worker keeps that restart in its dynamic extent while the controller inspects the problem.

visual.description: The worker holds the active restart

visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: Repair the helper and replace the report body
scenes.narration: Repair the category-label helper. Also define a new report body with a different marker. Those changes are provisional parts of the paused attempt until it completes safely.

scenes.title: The original call continues
scenes.narration: Resume through the live restart. The report completes with v-one active frame and an entry count of one. That result proves the original invocation continued.

scenes.title: The next call uses the new definition
scenes.narration: Call the report again. Now it returns v-two new frame and the entry count reaches two. New calls use the replacement; existing frames keep their original bodies.

visual.description: The next call uses the new definition
visual.headline: The next call uses the new definition

scenes.title: The caller defines success
scenes.narration: The caller supplies executable goals. For this ledger, the known expenses must total fifty-four dollars and fifty cents, and the sixty dollar report must leave five dollars and fifty cents. Model-written tests cannot replace that contract.

visual.description: The caller defines success
visual.headline: The caller defines success
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: Safety checks protect intermediate state
scenes.narration: Safety invariants answer another question: is the managed ledger still valid? A bad amount or malformed entry must fail the caller check. When safety fails, the attempt is rejected and managed changes are restored.

visual.description: Safety checks protect intermediate state
visual.headline: Safety checks protect intermediate state
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.

scenes.title: Safe progress can precede a finished feature
scenes.narration: A missing report can leave the goal false while a useful new helper is accepted. That allows incremental development. Goal predicates track completion; safety checks constrain every accepted step toward it. Inspect both in the demo evidence.

visual.description: Safe progress can precede a finished feature
visual.headline: Safe progress can precede a finished feature
visual.caption: Recorded kernel execution; see provenance label.
